context:
Goal: q_max's browser tier finishes, so main's browser read is known and merges are not blocked.
Problem (goal): the full tier is 672 checks and takes about 2 h 45 min to 3 h 10 min on a runner, over the 180 min cap; nothing hangs. 14-FLOSS alone is 40-45 min.
Based on (measured): run 40740294267 hit the cap at 2 h 59 min with 623 of 672 done; per-check times sum to 10,587 s of the step's 10,753 s.
Based on (read): D-542 (the browser tier runs on your dispatch) is unchanged by either option.
Departs from: q_max main (one browser job, 180 min cap) — a raises the cap to 240 min; b runs 14-FLOSS and 14-STILL as a second job with its own port and database.

Meanwhile: lane qmax-browser-tier-hang raises the cap to 240 min as a named bandaid, so a dispatched run can finish; lane qmax-browser-red-checks fixes the checks that fail.
home: q_max .github/workflows/browser.yml; D-542, the browser tier runs on your dispatch

options.gain: No more work; a run finishes.
options.how: No more work after the bandaid lane.
options.label: Keep one job at the new 240 min cap
options.lose: Each dispatch takes about 3 h of runner time and your wait.

options.how: A build lane moves 14-FLOSS and 14-STILL to a second job with its own port and database, each with its own count check.
options.label: Split into two parallel jobs
options.lose: A build lane; each job needs its own count check, because a filtered run turns the count check off; the same total runner minutes.

title: q_max: split the browser tier into two jobs, so a run takes about 2 h instead of 3?
why: Recommended: a. The run finishes with no more work; b saves wait time but costs a build lane and the same runner minutes.
